text: My doctor put me on a GLP-1 and never once mentioned what it does to your gut. I had to figure that out myself at 10:00 AM on a Tuesday when I genuinely could not shit. Let me tell you what she never told me, because nobody told me either. The shot was working and I was dropping weight, but I felt like someone had filled my gut with concrete and forgotten about it. I'd eat a few bites at dinner and feel like I'd swallowed a brick. My jeans were getting looser, but I was still leaving the dinner table early. Everyone kept telling me how great I looked, and I couldn't explain it to anyone without sounding dramatic because from the outside, everything was working and I genuinely thought losing the weight would fix it. My doctor told me to add more fiber, so I started mixing fiber powder into my water every morning and eating high fiber everything. I gave it a couple of months and if anything, I felt worse, still waking up every morning with my gut full of yesterday. So I went to the pharmacy and got Miralax, and that felt like admitting something had genuinely gone wrong. I stood in that aisle thinking, "I shouldn't need this," but I was desperate enough that I didn't care. It helped a little, but the moment it wore off, I was right back where I started. Something was still missing. So I started doing a crazy amount of research. I must have read thirty articles, forums, medical breakdowns, all of it. And then I came across a gastroenterologist who explained exactly what GLP-1s do to the gut. He explained it like this: your stomach is basically a muscle that contracts and pushes everything forward, but GLP-1s slow those contractions down. Think of a river slowing to a trickle. Everything behind it starts to back up. Food, waste, gas with nowhere to go, and all that pressure is what you're feeling every day. It wasn't a diet problem, and it wasn't something I was doing wrong. It was the gut slowdown and my mind started racing. Was this why the fiber never did anything? Why Miralax only worked until it wore off? So now I knew what was causing it, but I had no idea what actually fixed the slowdown. One night I was up late scrolling a GLP-1 support group on Facebook, and a woman posted that she'd been backed up for months on Ozempic until she started using three specific ingredients together. First was apigenin from celery juice, which she said has been shown to activate the receptors in the gut wall that trigger those contractions. Second was chlorophyllin, a plant compound that binds gas-producing compounds before they build pressure. Third was a soluble prebiotic fiber, and she was specific about the type. The bulk kind in most fiber powders and gummies just piles up in a gut that's already slowed down, which is exactly why mine made things worse. She said that's why Miralax never stuck for her either. It's just pushing stuff out. This is actually getting the muscle to start moving again on its own. She'd been on the shot for a year and said it was the only thing that ever worked. She'd finally stopped dreading meals. I almost kept scrolling because I'd tried the celery juice thing back in twenty nineteen and felt nothing. But she said it doesn't work on its own. You need all three together in the right ratio. She linked the one she used, it's called Motili, and it was the only one I could find with all three in the same gummy. Everything else was just fiber with a different label. So I ordered it and changed nothing else. Same shot, same eating. Two gummies before breakfast with a glass of water. The first week, honestly, nothing happened. But by week two, I was sitting through a full dinner with my husband without that pressure building once. And by week six, I realized I hadn't thought about my stomach in days. That was me two months ago. Now I get through dinner without planning my exit, and I'm not mapping my day around when I might feel okay. So if you're on a GLP-1, losing the weight and still waking up every morning backed up and wondering why nobody warned you, this is why. I'll drop the link below. If ninety days in, it's not the difference you were hoping for, they give you all your money back.
